simple.meaning: רֹעַ (rôaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “badness (as marring ), physically or morally.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 19 times in Genesis, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, Nehemiah, Psalms, and 4 more, beginning at Genesis 41:19. The surrounding contexts include family, kingship, land, wilderness, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֹעַ (H7455) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רֹעַ (rôaʻ) / H7455 is traced through Genesis 41:19, Deuteronomy 28:20, 1 Samuel 17:28, Nehemiah 2:2 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.usage: × be so bad, badness, (× be so) evil, naughtiness, sadness, sorrow, wickedness.
definitions.full: H7455. roa רֹעַ noun [masculine] badness, evil ; — ׳ר absolute Gen 41:19 4 t. Jeremiah; construct Hosea 9:15 13 t.; — 1 badness, bad quality , of cattle Gen 41:19 (E), figs Jer 24:2-3 , 8 ; 29:17 . 2 wilfulness , לבב רֹעַ 1Sam 17:28 (Gerber 161makes 2 and 4 [infinitive of] verb). 3 ethical , evil, badness , only in phrase: מעללים רֹעַ evil of doings Deut 28:20 ; Isa 1:16 ; Jer 4:4 ; 21:12 ; 23:2 , 22 ; 25:5 ; 26:3 ; 44:22 ; Hosea 9:15 ; Psa 28:4 (compare מעללים רַע 1Sam 25:3 ). 4 sadness , ׳ר מָּנִים Eccl 7:3 , ׳ר לֵב Neh 2:3 (compare [ רָעַע ] 2 ).

occurrences.englishText: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

Yahweh will send on you cursing, confusion, and rebuke in all that you put your hand to do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your doings, by which you have forsaken me.

Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men; and Eliab’s anger burned against David, and he said, “Why have you come down? With whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride, and the naughtiness of your heart; for you have come down that you might see the battle.”
The king said to me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart.”
Give them according to their work, and according to the wickedness of their doings.
Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.

Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh, and take away the foreskins of your heart, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem; lest my wrath go out like fire, and burn so that no one can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.

Therefore Yahweh, the God of Israel, says against the shepherds who feed my people: “You have scattered my flock, driven them away, and have not visited them. Behold, I will visit on you the evil of your doings,” says Yahweh.
But if they had stood in my council,
One basket had very good figs, like the figs that are first-ripe; and the other basket had very bad figs, which could not be eaten, they were so bad.
Then Yahweh asked me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?”

“ ‘As the bad figs, which can’t be eaten, they are so bad,’ surely Yahweh says, ‘So I will give up Zedekiah the king of Judah, and his princes, and the remnant of Jerusalem, who remain in this land, and those who dwell in the land of Egypt.
saying, “Return now everyone from his evil way, and from the evil of your doings, and dwell in the land that Yahweh has given to you and to your fathers, from of old and even forever more.
It may be they will listen, and every man turn from his evil way; that I may relent from the evil which I intend to do to them because of the evil of their doings.’
Yahweh of Armies says: “Behold, I will send on them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and will make them like rotten figs that can’t be eaten, they are so bad.

Thus Yahweh could no longer bear it, because of the evil of your doings, and because of the abominations which you have committed. Therefore your land has become a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is today.
